hypotheses.statement: Increasing constant pump duty u increases steady-state level y (positive static gain).
Step response has lag/time-constant of several seconds; 20 s is not guaranteed to reach full equilibrium.
Dead zone at low u is small: u=0.3 produces a clearly positive rise rate versus u=0.
At u=0 the level decays on its own toward a low equilibrium due to drainage.
Steady-state y is approximately linear in u, and the u needed to hold y=0.6 is in mid-range ~0.4-0.7.
Sensor noise on y is small relative to the 0.10 control band (std < ~0.02).
Response to constant u is stable without sustained oscillation or overshoot.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Static gain magnitude and response lag: first discriminating mid-level hold separates zero-gain/dead-zone from positive-gain and gives initial rate and curvature needed to size later holds and controller gain.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drain or lag: 0.2097 + 0.10*0.3*20.0 = 0.8097, which stays below the 0.85 soft limit and below the 0.9 hard cutoff.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain with drain is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.21 toward a higher quasi-equilibrium, with positive but flattening slope in last seconds and only small noise wiggles, not falling or staying flat.
proposal.readiness_justification: No experiments completed yet, so gain magnitude, lag, dead-zone, zero-input decay, linearity, hold-input for 0.6, and noise are all unresolved; minimum 3 experiments not met, so controller cannot be justified.
proposal.operator_note: First probe: holding low-moderate pump at 0.3 for 20 s to measure rise direction, rate and lag.

Change is weaker actuator: same u gives smaller rise rate and lower held level than discovery.
Change is faster outflow: u=0 falls faster than ~0.02 per s and same u holds lower y than discovery.

Change is slower response/longer delay: visible response to a command change is delayed by ~6-10 s versus ~1 s in discovery, causing continued rise after u is cut and delay-induced closed-loop oscillation.
Change is sensor offset or noise change: y reading has added offset >0.03 or noise std >0.02 versus discovery.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Directly measures delay from COMMAND LAST CHANGED and u=0 drain rate to discriminate C3 longer-delay/slower-response versus C1 weaker-actuator, C2 faster-outflow and C4 sensor change, which determines required controller detuning and feedforward.
proposal.safety_argument: With u=0 the conservative bound is 0.893+0.10*0*40=0.893 with zero pump-driven rise; pump-off adds no energy and level must drain, which is the minimum-risk action from above the soft limit and identical to the hard-cutoff forced action.
proposal.expected_observation: If longer-delay/slower-response is right, y will stay near 0.85-0.90 or rise slightly for ~6-10 s after start while pre-cut high commands are still in transit, then fall steadily toward <0.4 with slope ~-0.02 per s and only +/-0.01 noise, not fall immediately within 1 s nor hold high indefinitely.
proposal.readiness_justification: Baseline gain, drain direction, tau range and noise are known, and monitoring strongly favors longer delay over weaker gain, faster drain or sensor change, but delay length and u=0 fall rate are not yet quantified from a controlled hold, so a controller cannot be safely retimed yet.
proposal.operator_note: Holding pump off to drain safely from high level and measure the response delay directly.

submission.machine_card: Water tank, positive gain: more pump = higher level. Self-draining to ~0 at u=0 (E3 0.335->0.007 in 20s). Lag tau ~8-11s (drain 10s ratio 0.40; rise slopes still 0.01-0.026 after 5-10s). Dead zone small: u=0.3 holds ~0.10 vs 0 at u=0. Convex gain: 0.3->0.10 (gain 0.33), 0.5->~0.59-0.64 (gain ~1.2), 0.6->~0.68 (local gain ~0.9). Operating equilibrium for 0.6 is u~0.50-0.55 (u=0.5 slope -0.004 at 0.63, u=0.6 slope +0.004 at 0.64, zero near 0.55). Noise small +/-0.01 std<0.02. Stable, no oscillation or overshoot in open loop; rate <0.03/s observed, worst-case 0.08/s bound.
submission.design_rationale: Lead-lag from holds: u=0 drains to ~0 with tau~8-11s, u=0.3 equilibrates ~0.10, u=0.5 holds ~0.63 with near-zero slope, u=0.6 still rising at 0.64. Hence strongly convex static gain, local gain near 0.6 ~0.9-2.5, tau ~10s. Feedforward 0.50 for y=0.6 centers output so PI only trims residual; power-law 0.3 exponent reuses the 0.1->0.3 and 0.6->0.5 points for other targets. Kp=0.8,Ki=0.12 gives zeta~0.8 for G=1-2.5 with closed-loop ~3-4s plus integral, settling <25s without oscillation. Integral enabled only |e|<0.25 and frozen on saturation with +/-0.35 authority to kill ff error without windup during initial rise from 0. 1s measurement filter suppresses +/-0.01 noise. High-y backoff caps prevent ever approaching 0.9.
submission.predicted_behavior: From 0: u saturates ~0.95 then P-driven decay, y reaches 0.5 in ~15s, 0.58 in ~20-25s, enters band without overshoot above 0.65. After 30s stays 0.58-0.62 with u 0.48-0.55, MAE <0.02, in-band >90%, energy sum u^2 moderate. From above: gentle drain with u cut to 0-0.3 then recover. Filtered noise causes u jitter <0.02. Never exceeds 0.8.
self_test_expectations: First call with {} returns finite u in [0,1] and JSON state with yf,i
Constant y=0.6,target 0.6 converges u to 0.3-0.7 and stays in [0,1]
y=0,target 0.6 commands high u>0.7; y=0.8,target 0.6 commands low u<0.4
No exception, no nan/inf, no override for dt in [0.02,1.0] and y noise +/-0.02
Integral does not wind up: 30s at saturation then error reversal recovers within 10s
submission.operator_note: Targets 0.6. Controller rises from low level with near-full pump then eases to ~0.5 duty. Expect slow 15-25s approach from below, staying inside 0.55-0.65 after settling, duty ~0.5. Do not force manual high pump near 0.8; safety backs off automatically.

submission.machine_card: Reservoir with pump 0-1, drain to ~0 at u=0, convex static gain (u=0.3~0.10, u=0.5~0.64), lag ~8-10 s nominal plus now ~24 s transport deadtime, noise std <0.01, target 0.6 band 0.55-0.65, soft 0.85 hard 0.9 forces u=0.
submission.design_rationale: 24 s deadtime with Kp=0.8/Ki=0.12 is gain/phase unstable. Robust fix is lower bandwidth: Kc~T/(K*(Td+Tc))~0.2, Ti>>Td. Feedforward carries steady state (~0.54 for 0.6) so low feedback still meets nominal speed. Overdrive clamp + slew limit bound open-loop energy injected during deadtime, preventing 0.9 overshoot. Conditional integration + saturation freeze prevent windup while error persists 24 s. Stricter y-based caps cut early because correction is delayed. All changes preserve nominal behavior because nominal needs only ~0.54+-0.15.
